passages.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
passages.sermon: Children must obey their parents.\r\nThey must do this in the Lord.\r\nThis is the right thing to do.
passages.original: Τὰ τέκνα ὑπακούετε τοῖς γονεῦσιν ὑμῶν ἐν Κυρίῳ τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν δίκαιον

passages.text: “Honor your father and mother” (which is the first commandment with a promise), “that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth.”
passages.sermon:
God gave a commandment to people.
God said, “Honor your father and mother.”
This commandment is the first one that includes a promise.
God promises something if you obey this commandment.
If you honor your father and mother, things will go well for you.
If you honor your father and mother, you will have a long life on the earth.
passages.original: Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη ἐν ἐπαγγελίᾳ Ἵνα εὖ σοι γένηται καὶ ἔσῃ μακροχρόνιος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: Fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath; instead, bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Fathers, do not make your children angry.
Do not provoke your children to wrath.
Instead, raise your children in the discipline of the Lord.
Teach your children the instruction of the Lord.
Bring up your children with the Lord’s guidance.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ πατέρες μὴ παροργίζετε τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἀλλὰ ἐκτρέφετε αὐτὰ ἐν παιδείᾳ καὶ νουθεσίᾳ Κυρίου

passages.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear and sincerity of heart, just as you would obey Christ.
passages.sermon:
Slaves must obey their earthly masters.
Slaves should show respect and fear to their masters.
Slaves must obey with sincerity of heart.
Slaves should obey their masters as they would obey Christ.
passages.original: Οἱ δοῦλοι ὑπακούετε τοῖς κατὰ σάρκα κυρίοις μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐν ἁπλότητι τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς τῷ Χριστῷ

passages.text: And do this not only to please them while they are watching, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from your heart.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to slaves and servants.
He tells them how to obey their earthly masters.
Do not obey only when your masters are watching you.
Do not act just to please people.
Instead, serve as servants of Christ.
Do the will of God from your heart.
passages.original: μὴ κατ’ ὀφθαλμοδουλίαν ὡς ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι ἀλλ’ ὡς δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ ποιοῦντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκ ψυχῆς

passages.text: Serve with good will, as to the Lord and not to men, because you know that the Lord will reward each one for whatever good he does, whether he is slave or free.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to slaves and masters in the church.
He tells slaves how to serve their earthly masters.
Serve with good will.
Serve as if you are serving the Lord.
Do not serve as if you are serving people.
Know this truth.
The Lord will reward each person for any good he does.
This is true for slaves.
This is also true for free people.
passages.original: μετ’ εὐνοίας δουλεύοντες ὡς τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις εἰδότες ὅτι ἕκαστος ἐάν τι ποιήσῃ ἀγαθόν τοῦτο κομίσεται παρὰ Κυρίου εἴτε δοῦλος εἴτε ἐλεύθερος

passages.text: And masters, do the same for your slaves. Give up your use of threats, because you know that He who is both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no favoritism with Him.
passages.sermon:
Masters, treat your slaves in the same way.
Do not threaten them.
You know that their Master is in heaven.
Your Master is also in heaven.
God does not show favoritism.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ κύριοι τὰ αὐτὰ ποιεῖτε πρὸς αὐτούς ἀνιέντες τὴν ἀπειλήν εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ αὐτῶν καὶ ὑμῶν ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ προσωπολημψία οὐκ ἔστιν παρ’ αὐτῷ

passages.text: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians.
He tells them what to do next.
Be strong in the Lord.
Rely on the Lord’s mighty power.
passages.original: Τοῦ λοιποῦ ἐνδυναμοῦσθε ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil’s schemes.
passages.sermon:
God gives you armor.
This armor is complete.
Put on the full armor of God.
The devil has schemes.
You must stand against the devil’s schemes.
You can stand when you wear God’s armor.
passages.original: ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι ὑμᾶς στῆναι πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου

passages.text: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world’s darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
passages.sermon:
We are Christians.
We face a struggle.
Our struggle is not against flesh and blood.
We do not fight against people.
We fight against rulers.
We fight against authorities.
We fight against the powers of this world’s darkness.
We fight against spiritual forces of evil.
These evil forces are in the heavenly realms.
passages.original: ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν ἡ πάλη πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὰς ἀρχάς πρὸς τὰς ἐξουσίας πρὸς τοὺς κοσμοκράτορας τοῦ σκότους τούτου πρὸς τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις

passages.text: Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand.
passages.sermon:
God gives His people spiritual armor.
This armor protects against evil.
Take up the full armor of God.
The day of evil will come.
You must be ready to stand your ground.
Do everything you can to prepare.
After you have done all, stand firm.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἀναλάβετε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα δυνηθῆτε ἀντιστῆναι ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πονηρᾷ καὶ ἅπαντα κατεργασάμενοι στῆναι

passages.text: Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed, and with your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Ephesus.
He tells them to stand firm.
He tells them to put on the belt of truth.
He tells them to fasten it around their waist.
He tells them to put on the breastplate of righteousness.
He tells them to wear it on their chest.
He tells them to put shoes on their feet.
He tells them to be ready with the gospel of peace.
passages.original: στῆτε οὖν περιζωσάμενοι τὴν ὀσφὺν ὑμῶν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸν θώρακα τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης

passages.text: In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
passages.sermon:
Take up the shield of faith.
You need the shield of faith in every situation.
The shield of faith will protect you.
The evil one will attack you with flaming arrows.
You can extinguish all these arrows with the shield of faith.
passages.original: ἐν πᾶσιν ἀναλαβόντες τὸν θυρεὸν τῆς πίστεως ἐν ᾧ δυνήσεσθε πάντα τὰ βέλη τοῦ πονηροῦ τὰ πεπυρωμένα σβέσαι

passages.text: And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
passages.sermon: Take the helmet of salvation.\r\nTake the sword of the Spirit.\r\nThe sword of the Spirit is the word of God.
passages.original: καὶ τὴν περικεφαλαίαν τοῦ σωτηρίου δέξασθε καὶ τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ Πνεύματος ὅ ἐστιν ῥῆμα Θεοῦ

passages.text: Pray in the Spirit at all times, with every kind of prayer and petition. To this end, stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers for all the saints.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians.
He tells them to pray.
Pray at all times.
Pray in the Spirit.
Use every kind of prayer.
Use every kind of request.
Stay alert.
Keep praying with perseverance.
Pray for all the saints.
passages.original: διὰ πάσης προσευχῆς καὶ δεήσεως προσευχόμενοι ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ ἐν Πνεύματι καὶ εἰς αὐτὸ ἀγρυπνοῦντες ἐν πάσῃ προσκαρτερήσει καὶ δεήσει περὶ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων

passages.text: Pray also for me, that whenever I open my mouth, words may be given me so that I will boldly make known the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains. Pray that I may proclaim it fearlessly, as I should.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an ambassador for the gospel.
Paul is in chains.
Pray for Paul.
Pray that God will give Paul words to speak when he opens his mouth.
Pray that Paul will boldly make known the mystery of the gospel.
Pray that Paul will proclaim the gospel fearlessly.
Paul should speak the gospel with courage.
passages.original: καὶ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ἵνα μοι δοθῇ λόγος ἐν ἀνοίξει τοῦ στόματός μου ἐν παρρησίᾳ γνωρίσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ὑπὲρ οὗ πρεσβεύω ἐν ἁλύσει ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ παρρησιάσωμαι ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι

passages.text: Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything, so that you also may know about me and what I am doing.
passages.sermon:
Tychicus is a beloved brother.
Tychicus is a faithful servant in the Lord.
Tychicus will tell you everything about me.
Tychicus will tell you what I am doing.
You will know about me and my actions because of Tychicus.
passages.original: Ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ κατ’ ἐμέ τί πράσσω πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ πιστὸς διάκονος ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
passages.sermon:
Tychicus is a beloved brother.
Tychicus is a faithful servant in the Lord.
I have sent Tychicus to you.
I sent him for this very purpose.
He will tell you about us.
He will encourage your hearts.
passages.original: ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἵνα γνῶτε τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν

passages.text: Peace to the brothers and love with faith from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God the Father gives peace.
The Lord Jesus Christ gives peace.
God the Father gives love with faith.
The Lord Jesus Christ gives love with faith.
God gives these gifts to the brothers.
passages.original: Εἰρήνη τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καὶ ἀγάπη μετὰ πίστεως ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an undying love.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians who love Jesus Christ.
Paul calls Jesus Christ our Lord.
Paul speaks about grace.
Paul says, “Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ.”
Paul describes this love as undying.
Paul gives grace to everyone who loves Jesus Christ with an undying love.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἀγαπώντων τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ
